name: BatchCalc
description: Production planning, inventory, and orders app — Orders, Calculation, Inventory, Production Runs, and Products modules.
purpose: Give production planning its own dedicated calculation/inventory tool, explicitly kept separate from her other apps.
notes: In daily use. Calculation deliberately mirrors WEB OPS's real capsule-calculation logic (same eight directions, field labels, rounding) rather than reinventing it. Inventory's core rule: a transfer is never a loss — yield is measured on produced() = current + drawn, not on what's left, so a fully-drawn batch doesn't misread as a total loss. A push to main migrates production (vercel-build runs prisma migrate deploy), so pushes are hers to run. Vercel Deployment Protection is still on, which blocks the operator tier behind Vercel's own login — flagged to her twice, not yet turned off. Local dev shares port 3019 with the agri-econ-platform project (an accidental collision, not fixed).

notes: Three roles: employees clock in/out and take breaks at a shared kiosk (badge number + 4-digit PIN), managers and super admins sign in with a password. Dashboard, live monitor, attendance, breaks, corrections, scheduler, tasks, employees, reports (CSV/XLSX/PDF export), audit, self-service password change, leave & absence management, and break-overrun reporting all shipped. name: PowerWatch
description: Absence-of-heartbeat mains power failure monitoring for industrial devices with no battery or UPS.
purpose: Detect a power failure the instant it happens for a device that can't signal its own outage, by watching for the absence of its heartbeat instead.
notes: Pure-core/adapter-shell architecture: src/core has no I/O and an injected clock, so detection logic is replayable and testable at 1000x speed; storage/queue/alerting/LLM are all adapters that degrade gracefully and report their degraded mode on /api/health. Vercel serverless can't run a long-lived detection loop, so it's worked around with /api/cron/detect plus a stale-tick 503 on /api/health — the GitHub Actions */5 cron does NOT reliably fire (verified: zero scheduled runs over 21 minutes) and would blow the free Actions tier anyway, so as of the last check nothing external was actually driving the tick yet. Check HANDOVER.md before assuming detection is live.
